title: Dai dai
description: A current, high-energy collaboration for noticing how Spanish travels across borders and musical styles.
learningFocus: Movement, celebration, and the sound of conversational Spanish in a pop chorus.

lines.note: The informal command baila means dance.
Noche is feminine, so use esta.
Vamos is useful in travel and everyday conversation.

title: La graciosa
description: A playful track for hearing contemporary slang, rhythm, and Caribbean influence in a current hit.
learningFocus: Describing personality and recognizing la as the feminine article.

lines.note: Graciosa changes form to agree with a feminine noun or person.
Me gusta is a high-value phrase for preferences.
Pasó is the past tense of pasar.

title: Superestrella
description: A bright pop pick for practicing identity, confidence, and everyday descriptive words.
learningFocus: Adjectives, emphasis, and Spanish pop vocabulary from Spain.

lines.note: Soy comes from ser, to be.
Está comes from estar, used for a state or condition.
A common phrase for adding emphasis.

title: Despacito
description: A familiar reggaeton classic with clear, memorable vocabulary for rhythm and pace.
learningFocus: Adverbs, body movement, and the difference between despacio and despacito.

lines.note: A useful phrase for slowing down and progressing gradually.
The -ito ending can make a word sound smaller or softer.
Use this when asking someone to repeat something.

title: Bailando
artist: Enrique Iglesias feat. Descemer Bueno & Gente de Zona
description: A cross-regional Latin pop favorite for hearing different accents and learning action words.
learningFocus: The -ando form, movement verbs, and practical phrases for joining an activity.

lines.note: Estoy + -ando describes an action in progress.
Conmigo is the combined form of con and mí.
Sin means without.

title: Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido
description: A warm Colombian pop pick for practicing time words, introductions, and reflective conversation.
learningFocus: Before and after language, meeting people, and Colombian Caribbean sound.

lines.note: A compact time word that appears in many useful phrases.
The te ending points to the person being addressed.
Bonito changes to bonita when describing a feminine noun.

title: NUEVAYoL
description: A Puerto Rico-centered opener for noticing place names, identity, and contemporary island Spanish.
learningFocus: Place, belonging, and the way proper names become part of a song's vocabulary.

lines.note: The title stylizes Nueva York as NUEVAYoL.
A useful phrase for talking about where someone is from.
Gente is grammatically feminine even when it refers to a mixed group.

title: VOY A LLeVARTE PA PR
description: A travel-ready track for hearing the near-future construction and Puerto Rico shorthand in the title.
learningFocus: Ir a + infinitive, invitations, and the informal shortening pa' for para.

lines.english: I am going to take you
lines.note: Voy a + infinitive expresses a near-future plan.
The title shortens para to pa', a common informal spelling of speech.
A lively first-person plural command used for leaving together.

title: BAILE INoLVIDABLE
description: A salsa-leaning lesson for movement words and describing an experience you will remember.
learningFocus: Noun-adjective agreement and the vocabulary of dancing and memory.

lines.note: Inolvidable stays the same for masculine and feminine nouns.
Baila is the informal command form of bailar.
A high-frequency phrase for lasting memories.

title: PERFuMITO NUEVO
description: A sensory track for practicing descriptions, memory, and the small -ito ending.
learningFocus: Noun-adjective agreement and diminutive endings in everyday Spanish.

lines.note: Nuevo agrees with the masculine noun perfume.
Huele comes from oler, to smell.
The -ito ending can make poco sound smaller or softer.

title: WELTiTA
description: A collaboration for hearing warmth, repetition, and the playful spelling of contemporary Puerto Rican pop.
learningFocus: Short conversational phrases for returning, staying close, and making plans.

lines.note: Use de vuelta when someone or something comes back.
Quédate is an informal command built from quedarse.
Extrañar is especially common across Latin America.

title: VeLDÁ
artist: Bad Bunny, Omar Courtz & Dei V
description: A three-artist cut for practicing truth, confidence, and modern urban phrasing.
learningFocus: Questions, emphasis, and the difference between verdad and de verdad.

lines.note: A common phrase for adding emphasis.
Dime combines di, tell, with me.
Sin means without and takes no article here.

title: EL CLúB
description: A genre-shifting track for nightlife vocabulary and noticing how electronic production can meet plena.
learningFocus: Time expressions, invitations, and the everyday noun club.

lines.note: Club is masculine in this common use.
Toda agrees with the feminine noun noche.
Literally we see each other; it is a natural goodbye.

title: KETU TeCRÉ
description: A playful track for hearing a familiar Caribbean question in highly stylized typography.
learningFocus: Question words, pronouns, and informal spoken rhythm.

lines.note: The title stylizes this Puerto Rican conversational question.
A common phrase for shared context or emphasis.
Context determines whether this sounds literal or surprised.

title: BOKeTE
description: A compact vocabulary lesson built around a concrete Puerto Rican Spanish noun.
learningFocus: Concrete nouns, location phrases, and describing damage or openings.

lines.note: A boquete is a large opening, often in a wall or surface.
En means in or on depending on context.
Se cayó is the past form of caerse, to fall down.

title: KLOuFRENS
description: A stylized deep cut for noticing how artists bend spelling while keeping the surrounding language conversational.
learningFocus: Friendship vocabulary, possessives, and informal Puerto Rican slang awareness.

lines.note: Pana is a widely used informal word for friend in the Caribbean.
Míos agrees with the implied masculine plural group.
Estamos comes from estar and describes a current state.

title: TURiSTA
description: A reflective track that connects especially well with the Spanish curriculum's Peru travel theme.
learningFocus: Travel nouns, farewells, and the emotional difference between visiting and belonging.

lines.note: Turista is the same form for masculine and feminine.
A natural phrase for sending someone off.
Me voy comes from irse, to leave or go away.

title: CAFé CON RON
artist: Bad Bunny feat. Los Pleneros de la Cresta
description: A tradition-forward collaboration for food and drink vocabulary, celebration, and Puerto Rican plena.
learningFocus: Nouns with con, social invitations, and the language of a shared table.

lines.note: Con means with and connects the two nouns.
Salud literally means health and is used for a toast.
Amigos is masculine plural for a mixed group or male friends.

title: PIToRRO DE COCO
description: A cultural vocabulary card for exploring a Puerto Rican drink reference without needing a full translation.
learningFocus: Regional food and drink words, ingredients, and descriptive phrases.

lines.note: Pitorro is a Puerto Rican sugarcane spirit; coco means coconut.
Hecho is the past participle of hacer, to make.
Botella is a useful everyday noun for drinks and travel.

title: LO QUE LE PASÓ A HAWAii
description: A story-focused song for practicing what happened, indirect objects, and island context.
learningFocus: Past-tense questions and the phrase lo que, what or that which.

lines.note: Le marks the person or thing affected by the event.
A simple past-tense question for checking on a situation.
La isla is feminine, so use a la.

title: EoO
description: A dancefloor cut for short commands, movement, and listening for vowel sounds in a stylized title.
learningFocus: Commands, repetition, and high-frequency movement verbs.

lines.note: Ven is the informal command form of venir.
The accent marks the stressed syllable in this command.
Use otra vez when asking someone to repeat an action.

title: DtMF
description: The album's reflective title track for talking about memories, photos, and regret.
learningFocus: The imperfect past, conditional meaning, and emotionally useful memory vocabulary.

lines.english: I should have taken more photos
lines.note: Debí expresses a past obligation or regret; tirar fotos means take photos in Caribbean Spanish.
Tuve is the irregular preterite of tener, to have.
Arrepentirse is a reflexive verb for expressing regret.

title: LA MuDANZA
description: A high-energy closer for practicing change, movement, and the sound of Puerto Rican celebration.
learningFocus: Moving-house vocabulary, commands, and talking about a new chapter.

lines.note: Mudanza usually means moving house, not simply a trip.
Mudarse is the reflexive verb for changing homes.
Comienzo is a useful noun for starting a new chapter.

title: telepatía
album: Sin Miedo (del Amor y Otros Demonios) ∞
description: A learner-friendly favorite for talking about distance, connection, and imagined communication.
learningFocus: Frequency words, conditional meaning, and romantic vocabulary.

lines.note: The accent marks the final stressed syllable.
A useful phrase for travel, relationships, and remote communication.
Cada means each or every and does not change for gender.

title: fue mejor
album: Sin Miedo (del Amor y Otros Demonios) ∞
description: A bilingual collaboration for comparing the past with the present and expressing a clear preference.
learningFocus: The preterite of ser, comparisons, and reflective relationship language.

lines.note: Fue is the past form shared by ser and ir.
Ya no is a compact way to describe a changed situation.
Sin means without and ti is the stressed pronoun after a preposition.

title: qué te pedí//
album: Sin Miedo (del Amor y Otros Demonios) ∞
description: A bolero-informed lesson for polite requests, expectations, and strong question intonation.
learningFocus: The preterite of pedir and object pronouns in everyday questions.

lines.english: what did I ask you for?
lines.note: Pedí is the first-person preterite of pedir, to ask for.
Te and lo are object pronouns placed before dije.
A flexible phrase that can limit or soften a statement.

title: vaya con dios
album: Sin Miedo (del Amor y Otros Demonios) ∞
description: A warm, classic-sounding track for farewells, wishes, and formal-sounding expressions.
learningFocus: Subjunctive commands, prepositions, and expressions of goodwill.

lines.note: Vaya is a formal or polite command from ir, to go.

lines.english: I hope it goes well for you
lines.note: A very useful good-wish expression with the subjunctive.
A friendly everyday farewell.

title: Igual Que Un Ángel
description: A cross-border collaboration for comparisons, compliments, and listening across pop and música mexicana.
learningFocus: Comparisons with igual que and descriptive adjectives.

lines.note: Use igual que to compare people, things, or actions.
Ángel keeps its written accent on the first syllable.
Tan means so or as, depending on the comparison.

title: Labios Mordidos
description: A confident pop-reggaeton collaboration for body vocabulary, descriptive participles, and Colombian sound.
learningFocus: Body parts, past participles used as adjectives, and agreement.

lines.note: Mordidos agrees with the masculine plural noun labios.
Ven is the informal command of venir.
A useful phrase for confidence and encouragement.
